The lower right corner of the painting is inscribed with a square seal in white characters, "Miaoji Qiyi".　　The seventh year refers to the seventh year of the Republic of China (1918), when Xu Beihong was 23 years old.　　The picture depicts a flower-spotted tiger lying on a rock, turning its head and looking back from afar, its alert gaze not only expands the spatial sense of the picture, but also reveals the dominant spirit of the king of all animals.　　The tiger in this painting is colored in the traditional Chinese painting style of light coloring, and the dynamics of the tiger's desire to move and stop are outlined with fine, strong strokes, while the skin on the tiger's back is rendered in dark or light ochre and vine yellow, showing a fine, silky texture.　　In calligraphy, Xu Beihong was influenced by Kang Youwei, and he was good at Han and Wei calligraphy. Before he went to France, he received a gift from his friend Ma Heng (character Shuping), who was very happy with the fine topography of Han and Wei, so he carefully drew this picture as a thank you.
